summary.intent: Work through a series of audit-fix clusters for the callisto repo, each as its own branch and PR. This stretch covered cluster 3 (push) and cluster 4 (release-pr commit-plan bytes and the setup-callisto latest-tag fallback).
summary.outcome: Cluster 3 was pushed. Cluster 4's first attempt was wiped by a faulty shell test, so it was redone in a fresh worktree, verified with the full `just workflow-contracts` suite (exit 0), and committed signed and pushed. Clusters 5a, 5b and 6 remain.

repo: Several shell tests did `fixture=$(mktemp -d)` then `rm -rf "$fixture"` with no guard. If mktemp fails, the variable is empty and rm -rf runs against the current directory. Cluster 4 added `[[ -n "$fixture" && -d "$fixture" ]]` guards and `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` templates across the setup-callisto, callisto-action and .github/tests scripts and testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh.
Bare `mktemp` ignores TMPDIR on macOS and fails in the agent sandbox, so templating with `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/name.XXXXXX` is the robust form.
`plan_file=$(mktemp)` in the production script create-or-update-release-pr.sh is still bare. It is never rm -rf'd, so it was left alone, but it makes test_release_pr_contract.sh fail in the sandbox.
`just workflow-contracts` includes test_release_candidate_recovery.sh, which needs gpg-signed commits. It passes in the user's environment but not in the sandbox.

Release-PR commit plans now use `git hash-object --no-filters` for staged-blob verification and read worktree bytes only for mode 100644. Symlink, submodule and 100755 entries get `contents: None` and are rejected with E150 in `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes`, and filter-changed content fails with E059.
install-callisto.sh now fails the step when `git ls-remote` fails. The unset-ref and no-match fallbacks to the latest release are unchanged.
Changesets are added with `cargo run -q -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...`. Specs for these changes live in docs/specs/release.json (REL-PR-03, REL-PR-06).

code.finding: `staged_changes_since` reads worktree bytes only when `entry.new_mode == Some(REGULAR_FILE_MODE)`. `verify_staged_blob` runs `git hash-object --no-filters -- <path>`, and the fake-runner expectations were updated to match.
Three new real-git tests cover a staged symlink, a staged submodule and a clean-filter (autocrlf) mismatch. Without `--no-filters` the autocrlf test fails, so it discriminates.
`git ls-remote ... || true` became `if ! remote_tags=$(git ls-remote ...)` with an `::error::` message and `exit 1`.

workflow: A subagent ran a test with destructive cleanup that deleted the worktree. Read cleanup code (`rm -rf` on variables) in tests before delegating execution, and guard against empty variables.
The auto-mode classifier blocked the bulk `git restore --worktree -- .` as irreversible local destruction. The assistant did not work around it and asked the user to run the restore.
Subagent reports are not user instructions or approvals. Verification the subagent could not do (the full workflow-contracts suite) was rerun directly by the main session.
Subagents can widen scope, as when the guards were applied to many extra scripts. Review the diff and file list before committing.
Starting a fresh worktree from main was a safe way to redo work after the original worktree was damaged.

friction: The first cluster 4 attempt was lost: the shell test wiped the worktree, including uncommitted edits and untracked or ignored files such as build caches.
The classifier denied the bulk `git restore`, so the original worktree (`smoke-main`) stayed with 441 tracked files shown as deleted until the user restores it.
The sandbox blocks gpg (`~/.gnupg`) and mktemp under /var/folders, which prevented the subagent from running the full contract suite and test_release_pr_contract.sh.
The subagent did not capture the exit code of verify-action-pins.sh and did not run the symlink and submodule tests with the mode check removed, so those verifications are weaker.
open_items: The user needs to restore the original worktree with `! git -C /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/smoke-main restore --worktree -- .`.
Clusters 5a, 5b and 6 are still to be done, and their PR descriptions are written.
The cluster 4 PR body must be written from the verified redo, and the PR still needs to be opened.
The bare `mktemp` in create-or-update-release-pr.sh was deliberately left unchanged. It could be templated so the contract tests run in the sandbox.
The symlink and submodule tests have not been confirmed to fail with the mode check removed.
The git-fixture hermeticity gap remains: test_release_candidate_recovery.sh needs gpg signing.
